subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native trust-authority and provenance contract should OpenClaw memory use before untrusted or externally derived content can become durable recall context?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the authority model, config surface, storage schema, SDK/result contract, and retrieval policy define a security boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design native trust contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and define source, review, trust tier, expiration, and retrieval-policy semantics before implementation.

options.title: Stage provenance first
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42647 as the prerequisite for durable source attribution, then implement trust policy on top of that model.

options.title: Defer to external integrations
options.body: Document AKF/world-model-mcp-style adapters as optional prior art while leaving native memory trust enforcement out of default OpenClaw for now.

recommendation.title: Design native trust contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define source, review, trust tier, expiration, and retrieval-policy semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing signal from current memory-host SDK blame/history and prior review context on this issue.
